C8 Chevy Corvette ZR1 Races Ford Mustang Dark Horse, Someone Gets Rolled, Though Not By Much
12 photos
Photo: Import 2 Race / YouTube
Over the past few weeks, we have been thinking that it’s already been a decidedly long time since the good folks over at the racing-focused ' Import 2 Race ' channel on YouTube have not yet returned to their traditional venue - Island Dragway in Great Meadows, New Jersey.
Instead, they still have a passion for roll races. Instead of the feisty quarter-mile dragstrip skirmishes, we have gotten a treasure trove of 65-mph roll race battles, with all the high-speed ‘drama’ happening at the legendary Pocono Raceway , a 2.5-mile tri-oval track in Blakeslee, Pennsylvania. Well, this time around, the videographer makes a change of scenery.
So, they’re still not back at Island Dragway, but at least they are coming closer to home – they were on point for a quick stint at the 2026 Sunday Funday Mod2Fame event, which took place at an airport in Sullivan County, New York. It’s a 45-mph roll race showcase, on this occasion, as the airport runway isn’t like the massive Pocono Raceway
No worries, though, as the protagonists compensate: on one side is a crimson Ford Mustang Dark Horse of the S650 generation, rocking the iconic 5.0-liter Coyote V8 with 500 horsepower on tap. Its opponent, however, is a true supercar: the black menace is the C8 iteration Chevrolet Corvette ZR1, packing a brand-new 5.5-liter twin-turbo V8 and no less than 1,064 horsepower, which is more than twice the Dark Horse’s oomph.
Well, under such circumstances, it’s pretty clear that everyone knew the outcome in advance. However, one should always expect the unexpected when drag or roll races are involved, so let’s check out the outcome together. Hint: one car finishes up in front of the other by merely a car length, which is quite unexpected, indeed.
Anyway, as far as Ford is concerned, they’re not worried about the rivalry with Chevrolet anymore because the Camaro is retired, and it’s going to take a while before General Motors puts it back into production – sometime next year at the earliest, coming back on the same underpinnings as the next-generation Cadillac CT5 and an upcoming Buick sedan.
The C8 Chevrolet Corvette , meanwhile, has its work cut out for it because it has become truly expensive – almost like a European mid-engine sports car. Truthfully, it also has cool things to show for the money, like the mid-engine setup, the all-new 6.7-liter naturally aspirated V8 packing 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque for the base Stingray and the returning Grand Sport, or the 721-hp Grand Sport X performance hybrid that has replaced the E-Ray starting with the 2027 model year, among other things.
As for the Mustang, it has the 795-hp Dark Horse SC just waiting around the corner for Stellantis to bring back the Hellcat V8 into the latest Charger to complete the Hemi resurrection. Cool, right?
